title: Introduce steadyband autoscaler and throttle-reconciliation loop to reduce oscillation and preserve throughput SLAs
author: Nina Park
description:
Problem / motivation: we have observed repeated scale-down + throttle loops for medium-tenancy workloads where brief drops in incoming concurrency cause the autoscaler to shrink capacity, then a quick surge triggers throttles and a costly scale-up. This leads to transient SLA gaps and increased tail latency. Goal: add a minimal steadyband that preserves a small, continuously allocated throughput floor per pool and introduce a reconciliation loop that aligns the autoscaler's decisions with the gateway throttler/token pools to avoid conflicting signals.

What this PR does (single-string body): Adds a new 'steadyband' concept to the Dedicated autoscaler: steadyband is a per-pool, tunable throughput reservation (in rps-equivalent) that persists even during aggressive scale-downs. Implements an EWMA-based steadyband estimator that consumes recent sustained usage (90s window by default) and clamps to configured min/max fractions to limit oversize. The autoscaler now exposes steadyband as a separate topology weight used when computing desired replicas and headroom. Introduces a throttle-reconciliation controller that watches gateway token pool levels and autoscaler headroom decisions; when token pools are dropping while the autoscaler is concurrently scaling down, the reconciliation controller delays scale-downs and optionally triggers soft-burst allocations from the warm pool.

Key design notes: - Steadyband is opt-in per fleet via FleetSpec.steadyband.enabled + FleetSpec.steadyband.min_rps + FleetSpec.steadyband.max_fraction. Default off for backwards compatibility. - The EWMA smoothing alpha and observation window are configurable; defaults chosen to trade reactivity for stability. - Reconciliation loop runs periodically and implements hysteresis: it requires two consecutive conflicting-signal ticks to inhibit a scale-down to avoid needless dithering. - Soft-burst path leverages existing warmlet prewarming; we add a short-lived lease that can be charged back to fleet reservations. - Telemetry: new metrics (fleet_steadyband_target_rps, fleet_steadyband_effective_fraction, throttle_reconcile_block_count) and an alert rule template included in observability package. - Tests: unit tests for the estimator and reconciliation logic, integration test that simulates a sawtooth load (drop -> surge) to assert no SLA gap for 95th percentile latency, and a benchmark harness run showing median cost delta < 1.2% with improved 99th latency on representative workloads.

Checklist: - [x] Feature flag gated and off by default - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration scenario reproducer + assertion - [x] Documentation snippet for FleetSpec + examples - [x] Telemetry and alerting snippets - [x] Backwards compatibility checks

Risks and mitigation: risk of over-reserving capacity when operators misconfigure min_rps; mitigated by conservative defaults (disabled by default, min_rps=0, max_fraction=0.15) and clear console warnings. The reconciliation controller is isolated and will only delay scale-downs (never force scale-ups), minimizing blast radius.

Related tickets/PRs: ENG-8765 (steadyband design doc), ENG-8810 (throttle-reconciliation spike investigation), and internal spike pr-511202 which prototyped the estimator.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Nice approach — can you explain why EWMA window is 90s vs 120s? Concerned about noisy short bursts.

Nina Park (author): Chose 90s after running the sawtooth reproducer; 120s increased steadyband memory and caused slower reaction to sustained demand. Made alpha/configurable and added comment referencing the benchmark run. Added a CLI flag for experiments.
Priya Sethi: Please add an assertion in the integration test that throttle_reconcile_block_count increments when we see conflicting signals; also add a unit test for the hysteresis path.
Nina Park: Added both tests, and a small refactor to make the hysteresis window injectable for tests.
Daniel Wu: lgtm after tests and a minor nits fix on log verbosity (debug for per-pool messages).

release_notes: Introduce steadyband autoscaling concept (opt-in) to provide a minimal reserved throughput per fleet and a throttle-reconciliation controller to reduce scale-down/throttle oscillation. Disabled by default; see docs/steadyband.md for configuration and migration guidance.
